summary.name: Yap
summary.one_liner: Yap is a free, open source macOS dictation app that turns speech into text on-device and pastes it into whatever app you are using.
use_cases: dictating into terminal or browser fields
summary.what_it_does: Yap transcribes speech on the Mac using Apple's Speech framework, so audio stays on the device. You press a shortcut to start and again to stop, and it pastes the recognized text into the active field, including terminals and browsers. The shortcut can be a key combination or a single modifier key. Transcripts are saved locally, can be searched, and can be copied again. Once macOS has the speech model for your language, dictation works without an internet connection.
notable: Runs transcription on-device with Apple's Speech framework; audio never leaves the Mac
No account, no API key, and no telemetry
Press-to-start, press-to-stop shortcut that pastes into the active app
caveats: Offline use requires macOS to have downloaded the speech model for your language first
